discovery: Quantum cryptography: quantum key distribution based on the uncertainty principle and on entanglement

nominees.name: Charles H. Bennett
nominees.affiliation: IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center, Yorktown Heights, USA

nominees.name: Artur K. Ekert
nominees.affiliation: University of Oxford, UK, and Centre for Quantum Technologies, National University of Singapore

motivation: Bennett and Brassard (BB84) showed that the laws of quantum physics themselves—the no-cloning principle and the disturbance caused by measuring non-orthogonal states—can guarantee the secrecy of communication, and with colleagues performed the first experimental demonstration in 1989. Ekert (1991) independently discovered that entanglement and violation of Bell inequalities certify a shared secret key, linking the foundations of quantum mechanics directly to security and seeding device-independent cryptography. These discoveries created the field of quantum communication: they turned Bell tests from philosophical questions into operational resources, inspired teleportation, entanglement-based networks and satellite quantum links, and now underpin national quantum communication infrastructures worldwide. The 2022 Prize honoured the experiments establishing entanglement; this prize would honour the conceptual discovery that made quantum physics a guarantor of information security, among the most consequential physical insights of the past half-century.
